claim: PCBP2 was identified as a direct interactor of an intracellular retention motif through CLIP coupled to RNA pull-down and proteomic analysis.
source: Here, PCBP2 was identified as a direct interactor of an intracellular retention motif: CLIP coupled to RNA pull-down and proteomic analysis demonstrated that it binds to miRNAs embedding this motif and mutagenesis proved the binding specificity.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from CLIP, RNA pull-down, and proteomic analysis as described in the abstract and detailed in the results section.

claim: PCBP2 binds to miRNAs embedding the CELL retention motif.
source: Here, PCBP2 was identified as a direct interactor of an intracellular retention motif: CLIP coupled to RNA pull-down and proteomic analysis demonstrated that it binds to miRNAs embedding this motif and mutagenesis proved the binding specificity.
evidence: Supported by CLIP and RNA pull-down experiments showing PCBP2 binding to miRNAs with CELL motifs.

claim: Mutagenesis proved the specificity of PCBP2 binding to the CELL motif.
source: Here, PCBP2 was identified as a direct interactor of an intracellular retention motif: CLIP coupled to RNA pull-down and proteomic analysis demonstrated that it binds to miRNAs embedding this motif and mutagenesis proved the binding specificity.
evidence: Mutagenesis experiments demonstrated that mutations in the CELL motif impair PCBP2 binding.

claim: PCBP2 binding requires SYNCRIP as indicated by SYNCRIP knock-down experiments.
source: Notably, PCBP2 binding requires SYNCRIP, a previously characterized miRNA EV-loader as indicated by SYNCRIP knock-down.
evidence: SYNCRIP knockdown experiments showed that PCBP2 binding is dependent on SYNCRIP presence.

claim: SYNCRIP and PCBP2 may contemporarily bind to miRNAs as demonstrated by EMSA assays.
source: SYNCRIP and PCBP2 may contemporarily bind to miRNAs as demonstrated by EMSA assays and PCBP2 knock-down causes EV loading of intracellular microRNAs.
evidence: EMSA assays showed an ultrashift indicating concurrent binding of both proteins to miRNAs.

claim: PCBP2 knock-down causes EV loading of intracellular microRNAs.
source: SYNCRIP and PCBP2 may contemporarily bind to miRNAs as demonstrated by EMSA assays and PCBP2 knock-down causes EV loading of intracellular microRNAs.
evidence: Knockdown experiments showed increased miRNA loading into EVs when PCBP2 is silenced.

claim: Multiple proteins/miRNA interactions govern miRNA compartmentalization.
source: This evidence highlights that multiple proteins/miRNA interactions govern miRNA compartmentalization and identifies PCBP2 as a dominant inhibitor of SYNCRIP function in murine hepatocytes.
evidence: The study demonstrates interactions between PCBP2, SYNCRIP, and miRNAs that collectively determine miRNA localization.

claim: PCBP2 is a dominant inhibitor of SYNCRIP function in murine hepatocytes.
source: This evidence highlights that multiple proteins/miRNA interactions govern miRNA compartmentalization and identifies PCBP2 as a dominant inhibitor of SYNCRIP function in murine hepatocytes.
evidence: Functional experiments show that PCBP2 impairs SYNCRIP-mediated miRNA export into EVs.

claim: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) budding from cellular plasma membrane differ in size and origin, including exosomes (30–150 nm diameter) and microvesicles (≥50 nm diameter).
source: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) budding from cellular plasma membrane and differing for size and origin (e.g., exosomes, of 30–150 nm diameter and microvesicles, which diameter is ≥50 nm) (van Niel et al., 2022) are uptaken by neighboring as well as by distant recipient cells, thus transferring their specific informational cargo of molecules.
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from van Niel et al., 2022.

claim: EVs are uptaken by neighboring as well as by distant recipient cells, thus transferring their specific informational cargo of molecules.
source: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) budding from cellular plasma membrane and differing for size and origin (e.g., exosomes, of 30–150 nm diameter and microvesicles, which diameter is ≥50 nm) (van Niel et al., 2022) are uptaken by neighboring as well as by distant recipient cells, thus transferring their specific informational cargo of molecules.
evidence: This is established knowledge about EV function.

claim: EVs are considered a well-assessed route for donor cells to promote changes in gene expression and cell behavior of recipient cells in several pathophysiological processes.
source: Indeed, EVs are now considered a well-assessed route for donor cells to promote changes in gene expression and cell behavior of recipient cells in several pathophysiological processes (Mathieu et al., 2019; Montaldo et al., 2021).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to Mathieu et al., 2019 and Montaldo et al., 2021.

claim: The EV-cargo of miRNAs does not simply reflect the cell of origin content, but rather is defined by dynamic and selective cell-specific loading mechanisms.
source: Notably, concerning miRNAs, the EV-cargo does not simply reflect the cell of origin content, but rather is defined by dynamic and selective cell-specific loading mechanisms (Garbo et al., 2024; Garcia-Martin et al., 2022; Mori et al., 2019; Santangelo et al., 2016; Villarroya-Beltri et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations describing selective miRNA loading mechanisms.

claim: The existence of multiple players controlling miRNA compartmentalization matches with the hypothesis of a multiprotein machinery that dynamically governs not only the EV sorting but also the intracellular retention of specific subsets of miRNAs.
source: The existence of multiple players controlling miRNA compartmentalization matches with the hypothesis of a multiprotein machinery that dynamically governs not only the EV sorting but also, conceivably, the intracellular retention of specific subsets of miRNAs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of multiple proteins involved in miRNA sorting.

claim: hnRNPA2B1 was the first identified RNA-binding protein that recognizes miRNAs containing the EXO motif (G/U,G,A/G/C,G/C) and guides their inclusion in EVs secreted by human primary T-lymphocytes.
source: In this regard, the first identified was the Heterogeneous Nuclear Ribonucleoprotein A2B1 (hnRNPA2B1), recognizing miRNAs containing the EXO motif (G/U,G,A/G/C,G/C) and guiding their inclusion in EVs secreted by human primary T-lymphocytes (Villarroya-Beltri et al., 2013).
evidence: This is cited from Villarroya-Beltri et al., 2013.

claim: SYNCRIP binds to miRNAs embedding a short hEXO motif (G/A/U,G/U/A,G/A/U,C/A/G,U/A,G/C) through its NURR domain and its RRMs recognizing the 5' of the motif.
source: A functional role was successively attributed to the Synaptotagmin-binding Cytoplasmic RNA-Interacting Protein (SYNCRIP or hnRNPQ) that, by binding to miRNAs embedding a short hEXO motif (G/A/U,G/U/A,G/A/U,C/A/G,U/A,G/C) through its NURR domain and its RRMs recognizing the 5' of the motif (Santangelo et al., 2016; Hobor et al., 2018), guides their inclusion in EVs secreted by hepatocytes.
evidence: This is cited from Santangelo et al., 2016 and Hobor et al., 2018.

claim: SYNCRIP guides miRNA inclusion in EVs secreted by hepatocytes.
source: A functional role was successively attributed to the Synaptotagmin-binding Cytoplasmic RNA-Interacting Protein (SYNCRIP or hnRNPQ) that, by binding to miRNAs embedding a short hEXO motif (G/A/U,G/U/A,G/A/U,C/A/G,U/A,G/C) through its NURR domain and its RRMs recognizing the 5' of the motif (Santangelo et al., 2016; Hobor et al., 2018), guides their inclusion in EVs secreted by hepatocytes.
evidence: This is cited from Santangelo et al., 2016 and Hobor et al., 2018.

claim: The hEXO motif increases the EV/cell ratio of miRNAs as demonstrated by the insertion of this sequence in a cell-retained miRNA.
source: Notably, hEXO was shown to increase the EV/cell ratio of miRNAs as demonstrated by the insertion of this sequence in a cell-retained miRNA (Santangelo et al., 2016; Hobor et al., 2018), thus paving the way for further manipulative perspectives in the growing field of RNA-based therapies (Garbo et al., 2022; Paunovska et al., 2022; Traber and Yu, 2023).
evidence: This is cited from Santangelo et al., 2016 and Hobor et al., 2018.

claim: Two RNA-binding proteins (ALYREF and FUS) have been characterized for export motifs.
source: While for these export motifs two RNA-binding proteins (ALYREF and FUS) have been characterized (Garcia-Martin et al., 2022) for the retention motifs, defined as 'CELL' (Garcia-Martin et al., 2022), as for the previously described 'CL' motifs (Villarroya-Beltri et al., 2013) the identification of interacting protein/s remains unaddressed.
evidence: This is cited from Garcia-Martin et al., 2022.

claim: For the retention motifs defined as 'CELL', the identification of interacting protein/s remained unaddressed prior to this study.
source: While for these export motifs two RNA-binding proteins (ALYREF and FUS) have been characterized (Garcia-Martin et al., 2022) for the retention motifs, defined as 'CELL' (Garcia-Martin et al., 2022), as for the previously described 'CL' motifs (Villarroya-Beltri et al., 2013) the identification of interacting protein/s remains unaddressed.
evidence: This establishes the gap in knowledge that the current study addresses.

claim: miRNA-155-3p was selected as bait for RNA pull-down due to the presence of the Core CELL-motif identified in AML12 cells.
source: Aiming to identify the RBPs involved in the intracellular retention, proteins from hepatocytes were used in RNA-pull-down by using as specific bait the miRNA-155-3p, selected for the presence of the Core CELL-motif identified in AML12 cells (Garcia-Martin et al., 2022; Figure 1A).
evidence: The selection is based on the presence of the CELL motif as identified by Garcia-Martin et al., 2022 and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Label-free nLC-MS/MS proteomic analysis identified 21 proteins enriched in miR-155-3p pull-down with respect to miR-155-3p mutated in the Core CELL motif.
source: Label-free nLC-MS/MS proteomic analysis allowed to identify miR-155-3p-interacting proteins (Supplementary file 1), and label-free quantification intensities analysis identified 21 proteins enriched in miR-155-3p pull-down with respect to miR-155-3p mutated in the Core CELL motif (miR-155-3p no-CELL) (Figure 1A, Supplementary file 2, and Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by proteomic data shown in Figure 1B and Supplementary files.

claim: Twelve of the 21 enriched proteins are classified as RNA-binding proteins, with six containing at least one canonical RNA-binding domain.
source: Twelve of them are classified as RNA-binding proteins, with six containing at least one canonical RNA-binding domain (Cook et al., 2011; Liao et al., 2020; Ray et al., 2013; Treiber et al., 2017, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is based on classification using established databases and literature.

claim: PCBP2 prefers CU-rich sequences.
source: For three of them, RNA-binding preferences are also known (i.e. PCBP2 prefers CU-rich sequences; Ray et al., 2013; Van Nostrand et al., 2020), LARP1 recognizes the CAP and the 5' top motif in mRNAs (Fonseca et al., 2015), and STAU1 binds to double-stranded RNAs (Wickham et al., 1999).
evidence: This is cited from Ray et al., 2013 and Van Nostrand et al., 2020.

claim: LARP1 recognizes the CAP and the 5' top motif in mRNAs.
source: For three of them, RNA-binding preferences are also known (i.e. PCBP2 prefers CU-rich sequences; Ray et al., 2013; Van Nostrand et al., 2020), LARP1 recognizes the CAP and the 5' top motif in mRNAs (Fonseca et al., 2015), and STAU1 binds to double-stranded RNAs (Wickham et al., 1999).
evidence: This is cited from Fonseca et al., 2015.

claim: STAU1 binds to double-stranded RNAs.
source: For three of them, RNA-binding preferences are also known (i.e. PCBP2 prefers CU-rich sequences; Ray et al., 2013; Van Nostrand et al., 2020), LARP1 recognizes the CAP and the 5' top motif in mRNAs (Fonseca et al., 2015), and STAU1 binds to double-stranded RNAs (Wickham et al., 1999).
evidence: This is cited from Wickham et al., 1999.

claim: PCBP2 interaction with miR-155-3p was confirmed by CLIP assay.
source: Among them, PCBP2 interaction with miR-155-3p was confirmed by CLIP assay (Figure 1C, left panel) and RNA pull-down followed by western blot analysis (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by CLIP data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: PCBP2 interaction with miR-155-3p was confirmed by RNA pull-down followed by western blot analysis.
source: Among them, PCBP2 interaction with miR-155-3p was confirmed by CLIP assay (Figure 1C, left panel) and RNA pull-down followed by western blot analysis (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by RNA pull-down data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: RNA pull-down confirmed the absence of interaction between PCBP2 and the CELL motif-devoid miR-365-2-5p.
source: A second proof of concept of the requirement of PCBP2/CELL motif interaction is provided by the observation on the CELL motif-devoid miR-365-2-5p (Figure 1C, middle panel); RNA pull-down confirmed the absence of interaction with PCBP2 (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by RNA pull-down data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The inclusion of the Core CELL motif in miR-365-2-5p allows PCBP2 interaction with this miRNA while maintaining SYNCRIP binding.
source: Notably, the inclusion of the Core CELL motif while maintaining SYNCRIP binding, allows PCBP2 interaction with this miRNA.
evidence: This is demonstrated by RNA pull-down experiments with mutated miR-365-2-5p.

claim: PCBP2 binding to miR-155-3p appears direct and sequence specific as demonstrated using a recombinant protein in RNA pull-down.
source: At least in vitro, this binding appears direct and sequence specific as demonstrated using a recombinant protein in RNA pull-down (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by RNA pull-down with recombinant PCBP2 shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Mutation of the CELL motif (miR-155-3p no-CELL) impairs PCBP2 binding.
source: The introduction of specific mutations allowed to test the requirement of the CELL motif since its modification (miR-155-3p no-CELL) impairs PCBP2 binding (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by RNA pull-down data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: miR-155-3p sequence contains the previously identified SYNCRIP binding site.
source: Notably, the inspection of the miR-155-3p sequence revealed the presence of the previously identified SYNCRIP binding site and both MS/MS analysis (Supplementary file 1) and CLIP assay (Figure 1G) confirmed SYNCRIP binding to this miRNA independently of the CELL motif mutation (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is confirmed by MS/MS analysis and CLIP assay shown in Figure 1G.

claim: SYNCRIP binds to miR-155-3p independently of the CELL motif mutation.
source: Notably, the inspection of the miR-155-3p sequence revealed the presence of the previously identified SYNCRIP binding site and both MS/MS analysis (Supplementary file 1) and CLIP assay (Figure 1G) confirmed SYNCRIP binding to this miRNA independently of the CELL motif mutation (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by CLIP and pull-down data shown in Figures 1D and 1G.

claim: The permutation of the downstream two nucleotides removing SYNCRIP-binding motif (miR-155-3p no-hEXO) impairs PCBP2 binding despite the conservation of the CELL retention motif.
source: Surprisingly, the permutation of the downstream two nucleotides removing SYNCRIP-binding motif (miR-155-3p no-hEXO, Figure 1A) impairs PCBP2 binding despite the conservation of the CELL retention motif (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by RNA pull-down data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: CLIP assay on miR-31-3p, embedding the sole CELL motif, indicates the absence of PCBP2 binding.
source: To test this hypothesis, CLIP assay was performed on miR-31-3p, embedding the sole CELL motif, indicating the absence of PCBP2 binding (Figure 1C, right panel).
evidence: This is demonstrated by CLIP data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: PCBP2 interference enhances miRNA-155-3p loading in EVs with respect to control cell-derived EVs.
source: Notably, PCBP2 interference (PCBP2 being not expressed in the EVs, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A) enhances miRNA-155-3p loading in EVs with respect to control cell-derived EVs (Figure 1H, left panel).
evidence: This is demonstrated by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: PCBP2 is not expressed in the EVs.
source: Notably, PCBP2 interference (PCBP2 being not expressed in the EVs, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A) enhances miRNA-155-3p loading in EVs with respect to control cell-derived EVs (Figure 1H, left panel).
evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: miR-365-2-5p (embedding the sole hEXO motif) is not differentially exported upon PCBP2 silencing.
source: As a further control that miRNAs without the CELL motif are not affected by PCBP2 silencing, the expression levels of miR-365-2-5p (embedding the sole hEXO motif) were analyzed in EVs and cells, and resulted not differentially exported (Figure 1H, middle panel).
evidence: This is demonstrated by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: SYNCRIP silencing reduces miR-155-3p export into EVs.
source: As expected, SYNCRIP silencing (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C and D) (expressed in both intracellular and EV compartment as shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A) reduces miR-155-3p export into EVs (Figure 1H, right panel; for EVs characterization, see Figure 1—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: SYNCRIP is expressed in both intracellular and EV compartment.
source: As expected, SYNCRIP silencing (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C and D) (expressed in both intracellular and EV compartment as shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A) reduces miR-155-3p export into EVs (Figure 1H, right panel; for EVs characterization, see Figure 1—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: PCBP2 or SYNCRIP knockdown does not affect EVs production.
source: Moreover, the effect of either PCBP2 or SYNCRIP knockdown on EVs production was ruled out by quantifying the number of EVs per cell in shPCBP2 or shSYNCRIP with respect to the shCTR conditions (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by EV quantification data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C.

claim: PCBP2 and SYNCRIP interact with each other.
source: First, we observed that the two proteins interact each other (Figure 2A) and more interestingly that both RBPs bind to miR-155-3p contemporarily as indicated by the ultra-shift obtained in EMSA assay (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Both PCBP2 and SYNCRIP bind to miR-155-3p contemporarily as indicated by the ultra-shift obtained in EMSA assay.
source: First, we observed that the two proteins interact each other (Figure 2A) and more interestingly that both RBPs bind to miR-155-3p contemporarily as indicated by the ultra-shift obtained in EMSA assay (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by EMSA data showing an ultrashift in Figure 2B.

claim: PCBP2 silencing does not affect SYNCRIP binding to miR-155-3p.
source: As shown in Figure 2C while PCBP2 silencing does not affect SYNCRIP binding, SYNCRIP silencing impairs also PCBP2 binding.
evidence: This is demonstrated by EMSA data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: SYNCRIP silencing impairs PCBP2 binding to miR-155-3p.
source: As shown in Figure 2C while PCBP2 silencing does not affect SYNCRIP binding, SYNCRIP silencing impairs also PCBP2 binding.
evidence: This is demonstrated by EMSA data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: SYNCRIP silencing impairs PCBP2 binding to miR-155-3p as shown by CLIP assay.
source: Furthermore, CLIP assay was performed on SYNCRIP-silenced cells; as shown in Figure 2D, SYNCRIP silencing impairs PCBP2 binding to miR-155-3p.
evidence: This is demonstrated by CLIP data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Mutagenesis of the sole hEXO motif (miR-26b-3p no-hEXO) on miR-26 backbone impairs PCBP2 binding.
source: To further confirm and extend this observation, a number of mutants were designed and tested by RNA pull-down for the binding capacity of these two proteins; results indicate that (i) mutagenesis of the sole hEXO motif (miR-26b-3p no-hEXO) on miR-26 backbone (bearing both hEXO and CELL motifs), impairs also PCBP2 binding (Figure 3A) and conversely (ii) the de novo inclusion of a hEXO motif in miR-31-3p backbone (bearing only CELL-motifs) (miR-31-3p+hEXO) confers a de novo PCBP2 binding ability to this mutant; furthermore, mutation in the CELL motif (miR-31-3p+hEXO no-CELL) impairs PCBP2 binding (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by RNA pull-down data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The de novo inclusion of a hEXO motif in miR-31-3p backbone (bearing only CELL-motifs) confers a de novo PCBP2 binding ability to this mutant.
source: To further confirm and extend this observation, a number of mutants were designed and tested by RNA pull-down for the binding capacity of these two proteins; results indicate that (i) mutagenesis of the sole hEXO motif (miR-26b-3p no-hEXO) on miR-26 backbone (bearing both hEXO and CELL motifs), impairs also PCBP2 binding (Figure 3A) and conversely (ii) the de novo inclusion of a hEXO motif in miR-31-3p backbone (bearing only CELL-motifs) (miR-31-3p+hEXO) confers a de novo PCBP2 binding ability to this mutant; furthermore, mutation in the CELL motif (miR-31-3p+hEXO no-CELL) impairs PCBP2 binding (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by RNA pull-down data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Mutation in the CELL motif (miR-31-3p+hEXO no-CELL) impairs PCBP2 binding.
source: To further confirm and extend this observation, a number of mutants were designed and tested by RNA pull-down for the binding capacity of these two proteins; results indicate that (i) mutagenesis of the sole hEXO motif (miR-26b-3p no-hEXO) on miR-26 backbone (bearing both hEXO and CELL motifs), impairs also PCBP2 binding (Figure 3A) and conversely (ii) the de novo inclusion of a hEXO motif in miR-31-3p backbone (bearing only CELL-motifs) (miR-31-3p+hEXO) confers a de novo PCBP2 binding ability to this mutant; furthermore, mutation in the CELL motif (miR-31-3p+hEXO no-CELL) impairs PCBP2 binding (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by RNA pull-down data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: PCBP2 binding requires both the CELL motif and SYNCRIP binding; in other words, SYNCRIP binding is epistatic to PCBP2 recruitment.
source: Overall, these data indicate that PCBP2 binding requires both the CELL motif and SYNCRIP binding; in other words, SYNCRIP binding is epistatic to PCBP2 recruitment.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple mutagenesis and knockdown experiments.

claim: NGS analysis of miRNAs exported in EVs produced by control and PCBP2-silenced murine hepatocytes allowed the selection of miRNAs differentially loaded in EVs in correlation to PCBP2.
source: First, NGS analysis of miRNAs exported in EVs produced by control and PCBP2-silenced murine hepatocytes allowed the selection of further miRNAs differentially loaded in EVs in correlation to PCBP2 (Supplementary file 3, Figure 4A and B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by NGS data shown in Figures 4A and 4B.

claim: PCBP2 silencing releases a SYNCRIP-dependent loading of miRNAs in the EVs.
source: In order to consider the possible impact of PCBP2 on miRNAs steady state level (resulting from variation in transcription and biogenesis), miRNA abundance in EVs and in the intracellular compartment was analyzed by qRT-PCR as EVs/cell ratio. Results indicate that PCBP2 silencing releases a SYNCRIP-dependent loading of miRNAs in the EVs (Figure 4D), thus highlighting a dominant PCBP2 cell-retention function on SYNCRIP-dependent export, evaluated on these miRNAs in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.
evidence: This is demonstrated by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Gene Ontology enrichment analysis of the PCBP2-dependent cell-retained miRNAs targets highlighted several biological pathways collectively influenced by these miRNAs (e.g., establishment of organelle localization, regulation of cell cycle, and lymphocyte differentiation).
source: Moreover, Gene Ontology (GO) enrichment analysis of the PCBP2-dependent cell-retained miRNAs targets have been performed (including both validated and predicted targets, respectively, obtained from TarBase v9.0 database and DIANA-microT web server). As reported in Figure 4E and in Figure 4—figure supplement 2, this analysis highlighted several biological pathways collectively influenced by these miRNAs (e.g., establishment of organelle localization, regulation of cell cycle, and lymphocyte differentiation).
evidence: This is demonstrated by GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 4E.

claim: T cells, NK cells and myeloid cells show a higher amount of IFN-γ production upon shPCBP2 EVs treatment in comparison to the shCTR EVs.
source: Specifically, as reported in Figure 4F, Figure 4—figure supplement 3, T cells, NK cells and myeloid cells show a higher amount of IFN-γ production upon shPCBP2 EVs treatment in comparison to the shCTR EVs; this suggests that PCBP2 silencing results in an EV-mediated modulation of the immune response.
evidence: This is demonstrated by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: PCBP2 silencing results in an EV-mediated modulation of the immune response.
source: Specifically, as reported in Figure 4F, Figure 4—figure supplement 3, T cells, NK cells and myeloid cells show a higher amount of IFN-γ production upon shPCBP2 EVs treatment in comparison to the shCTR EVs; this suggests that PCBP2 silencing results in an EV-mediated modulation of the immune response.
evidence: This is inferred from the increased IFN-γ production in immune cells treated with shPCBP2 EVs.

claim: CLIP-qPCR assay demonstrates PCBP2 binding to miRs-345-3p, 23a-5p, 214-3p, 155-5p, 181d-5p, 3084-5p, 122b-3p, 192-5p, 26b-3p that bear both the CELL and hEXO motifs.
source: With respect to the molecular mechanism, the analysis by CLIP-qPCR assay demonstrates the PCBP2 binding to miRs-345-3p, 23a-5p, 214-3p, 155-5p, 181d-5p, 3084-5p, 122b-3p, 192-5p, 26b-3p that bear both the CELL and hEXO motifs; conversely, the presence of either the sole hEXO (miR-365-2-5p) or the sole CELL (miR-31-3p, miR-195a-5p, miR-421-3p) does not allow PCBP2 binding (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by CLIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The presence of either the sole hEXO (miR-365-2-5p) or the sole CELL (miR-31-3p, miR-195a-5p, miR-421-3p) does not allow PCBP2 binding.
source: With respect to the molecular mechanism, the analysis by CLIP-qPCR assay demonstrates the PCBP2 binding to miRs-345-3p, 23a-5p, 214-3p, 155-5p, 181d-5p, 3084-5p, 122b-3p, 192-5p, 26b-3p that bear both the CELL and hEXO motifs; conversely, the presence of either the sole hEXO (miR-365-2-5p) or the sole CELL (miR-31-3p, miR-195a-5p, miR-421-3p) does not allow PCBP2 binding (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by CLIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The presence of hEXO motif alone or in combination with the CELL motif is sufficient for SYNCRIP binding to all the analyzed miRNAs.
source: As expected, the presence of hEXO motif alone or in combination with the CELL motif is sufficient for SYNCRIP binding to all the analyzed miRNAs (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by CLIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Results demonstrate the SYNCRIP-dependent PCBP2 binding assessed in hepatocytes silenced for SYNCRIP for multiple miRNAs.
source: Furthermore, in line with data obtained for miR-155-3p (see Figure 2D), results shown in Figure 6 demonstrate the SYNCRIP-dependent PCBP2 binding assessed in hepatocytes silenced for SYNCRIP.
evidence: This is demonstrated by CLIP data shown in Figure 6.

claim: The previously described SYNCRIP capacity to act as EV loader is functionally limited by the presence of a sequence- and SYNCRIP-dependent retention mechanism mediated by the RNA-binding protein PCBP2.
source: Overall, these data indicate that the previously described SYNCRIP capacity to act as EV loader is functionally limited by the presence of a here-identified sequence- and SYNCRIP-dependent retention mechanism mediated by the RNA-binding protein PCBP2.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the collective experimental evidence.

claim: PCBP2 binding requires both the miRNA CELL sequence and the RBP SYNCRIP, which in turn recognizes its specific hEXO consensus; in other words, SYNCRIP binding is a prerequisite for PCBP2 recruitment.
source: Evidence here gathered indicates that (i) PCBP2 binding requires both the miRNA CELL sequence and the RBP SYNCRIP, which in turn recognizes its specific hEXO consensus; in other words, SYNCRIP binding is a prerequisite for PCBP2 recruitment; (ii) PCBP2 cell retention function is dominant over the SYNCRIP-dependent EV-loading; in other words, PCBP2 impairs SYNCRIP-mediated miRNA export (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings supported by multiple experiments.

claim: PCBP2 cell retention function is dominant over the SYNCRIP-dependent EV-loading; in other words, PCBP2 impairs SYNCRIP-mediated miRNA export.
source: Evidence here gathered indicates that (i) PCBP2 binding requires both the miRNA CELL sequence and the RBP SYNCRIP, which in turn recognizes its specific hEXO consensus; in other words, SYNCRIP binding is a prerequisite for PCBP2 recruitment; (ii) PCBP2 cell retention function is dominant over the SYNCRIP-dependent EV-loading; in other words, PCBP2 impairs SYNCRIP-mediated miRNA export (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings supported by multiple experiments.

claim: SYNCRIP EV-loading activity has been previously well characterized by means of both functional and structural analysis.
source: While SYNCRIP EV-loading activity has been previously well characterized by means of both functional and structural analysis (Santangelo et al., 2016; Hobor et al., 2018), the role of PCBP2 as a mediator of miRNA intracellular retention is here disclosed for the first time.
evidence: This is cited from Santangelo et al., 2016 and Hobor et al., 2018.

claim: The role of PCBP2 as a mediator of miRNA intracellular retention is disclosed for the first time in this study.
source: While SYNCRIP EV-loading activity has been previously well characterized by means of both functional and structural analysis (Santangelo et al., 2016; Hobor et al., 2018), the role of PCBP2 as a mediator of miRNA intracellular retention is here disclosed for the first time.
evidence: This establishes the novelty of the current findings.

claim: No data were previously reported on the RBPs involved in miRNA cell retention even if the role of specific consensus sequences has been previously defined by means of functional assays involving the introduction/removal of the CELL motifs.
source: Indeed, no data were previously reported on the RBPs involved in miRNA cell retention even if the role of specific consensus sequences has been previously defined by means of functional assays involving the introduction/removal of the CELL motifs (Garcia-Martin et al., 2022).
evidence: This establishes the gap in knowledge that the current study addresses, with reference to Garcia-Martin et al., 2022.

claim: PCBP2 protein is a well-characterized member of the Poly‐rC‐binding proteins (PCBPs), a group of multifunctional RNA-binding proteins that contain three highly conserved RNA binding KH domains and that may shuttle between the nucleus and the cytoplasm.
source: PCBP2 protein (similarly to SYNCRIP) displays a pleiotropic function; specifically, it is a well-characterized member of the Poly‐rC‐binding proteins (PCBPs), a group of multifunctional RNA-binding proteins that contain three highly conserved RNA binding KH domains and that may shuttle between the nucleus and the cytoplasm (Yuan et al., 2021).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Yuan et al., 2021.

claim: PCBP2 plays a role in controlling multiple processes, including RNA maturation and trafficking, RNA editing, translational activation or repression, and mRNA degradation.
source: A large body of evidence points to its role in controlling multiple processes, including RNA maturation and trafficking, RNA editing, translational activation or repression, and mRNA degradation (Chaudhury et al., 2010; Ishii et al., 2020; Makeyev et al., 1999; Makeyev and Liebhaber, 2002; Perrotti et al., 2002; Yabe-Wada et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

source: Of note, among them, miRs-155-3p, 23a-5p, 155-5p, 192-5p, and 26b-3p display important EV-mediated functions in relation to pathophysiology (Broermann et al., 2020; Dosil et al., 2022; Jiao et al., 2021; Zhao et al., 2024), as also assessed by GO analysis.
